skill.name: personwise-sales-enablement-training
skill.description: Creates grounded PersonWise sales enablement courses from approved materials, with digital-human delivery, voice questions, checkpoint reviews, and controlled publishing.
skill.summary: Turn approved sales materials into an interactive, evidence-grounded readiness course.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, quoted shell substitutions, integrity checks, and signed descriptor data. The skill still installs an opaque third-party CLI, uploads local files, consumes existing credits, and may execute server-provided update commands. Stronger consent, destination disclosure, and command allowlisting are required.

remediation.issue: The workflow installs and runs a third-party executable that is not reviewable in this package.
remediation.suggestion: Require informed confirmation before installation, disclose the release origin, and publish reproducible source or an independently verifiable build provenance.

remediation.issue: Update action text returned by the service is executed as a command.
remediation.suggestion: Parse a structured action identifier, map it to a strict local command allowlist, and reject shell metacharacters or unexpected arguments.

remediation.issue: Selected local sales materials are uploaded without a separate destination disclosure.
remediation.suggestion: Show each file path, the PersonWise destination, and the data handling purpose before obtaining explicit upload confirmation.

remediation.issue: Course creation consumes existing credits without a separate confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Display the exact credit cost and require confirmation before each credit-consuming create action, especially during implicit invocation.

finding_verdicts.reason: The installer downloads one version-pinned archive over HTTPS with redirects disabled, then enforces exact size and SHA-256 values. The fixed release URL is expected installer behavior.
The substitution runs fixed uname commands to select a supported platform. No untrusted value controls the command or its arguments.
The substitution runs fixed uname output inside a platform guard. It does not evaluate user-controlled shell text.
The substitution runs fixed uname output to select the installation directory. No command injection path is present.
The substitution passes the quoted target directory through fixed printf and tr commands to reject control characters. Shell interpolation is quoted.
The substitution reads the quoted install directory inode for a later race check. It does not construct or execute a user-supplied command.
The substitution calls the local checksum helper on a quoted executable path. The helper uses fixed SHA-256 utilities and does not evaluate input.
The substitution creates a uniquely named temporary directory under the quoted install directory. mktemp is invoked directly without dynamic command text.
The substitution measures the downloaded archive with fixed wc and tr commands. The archive path is quoted and cannot alter command structure.
The substitution computes a SHA-256 digest through a fixed helper before extraction. No untrusted command name or shell evaluation is used.
The substitution lists a checksum-verified archive with tar so its entries can be compared against an exact allowlist. The archive path is quoted.
The substitution verifies the extracted executable with a fixed checksum helper. This is an integrity control, not dynamic command execution.
The substitution runs fixed uname output inside a macOS signature-verification guard. No untrusted text is evaluated by the shell.
The substitution invokes fixed macOS signing tools on the quoted candidate path and extracts the signing authority. No argument controls command syntax.
The substitution rechecks the quoted install directory inode to detect replacement during installation. This is a local race-defense check.
The substitution recomputes the quoted target executable checksum before replacement. It uses fixed commands and prevents concurrent modification.
The installer uses a version-pinned HTTPS release origin and verifies exact archive size, archive hash, contents, and executable hash before installation. The URL is not an exfiltration endpoint.
The script selects the conventional per-user executable directory under HOME and quotes the resulting path. It neither searches unrelated hidden data nor accesses credentials.

The dot-prefixed path is a dedicated mktemp workspace for an approved installation. A cleanup trap removes it, and it is not used to conceal persistent data.

mktemp creates a unique installation workspace, and a trap removes it on exit or interruption. This is bounded temporary storage for a verified archive.
The hard link atomically installs the already verified candidate only when the target is absent. Failure stops the installer, preventing overwrite of an occupied path.

content.value_statement: Sales teams struggle to convert approved launch materials into consistent, evidence-based training. This skill creates an interactive PersonWise course with grounded scripts, reviews, and learner questions.
actual_capabilities: Builds a sales-readiness teaching arc from approved positioning, proof, objections, and launch materials.
Creates interactive PersonWise courses with digital-human presentation and grounded voice questions.
Uploads user-selected source documents and tracks their processing status.
Reviews outline, script, slide text, and image checkpoints before advancing.
Resumes interrupted runs and applies bounded retries from current workflow state.
Publishes courses or changes access only when the requested target is authorized.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, service access, and available course credits.
Uploads selected source files to the external PersonWise service for processing.
Cannot support claims, customer evidence, pricing, or competitive statements absent from approved materials.
Cannot guarantee certification, learner competence, platform approval, or real-world completion.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Product Launch
use_cases.description: Convert approved launch messaging into a grounded course covering buyers, value, proof, objections, and practice.

use_cases.title: Standardize Sales Readiness
use_cases.description: Give representatives a consistent interactive course based on approved claims and current sales materials.

use_cases.title: Review Course Accuracy
use_cases.description: Inspect course checkpoints and correct unsupported claims, inconsistent scripts, or weak visual choices before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private sales enablement course from the attached launch materials. Use only supported claims and include buyer context, value, proof, objections, and practice.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has approved materials and needs a complete readiness course.

prompt_templates.title: Set a Page Limit
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a private sales readiness course from these documents in no more than eight slides. Recompose the teaching arc if my account limit is lower.
prompt_templates.scenario: A course must fit a specific delivery length.

prompt_templates.title: Use Strict Source Grounding
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only product launch course from the selected files. Flag unsupported claims and route pricing questions to our deal desk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Commercial or legal review requires strict source fidelity.

prompt_templates.title: Resume and Publish
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume the existing course run, review every checkpoint, fix objective grounding issues, and publish with link access after current state confirms readiness.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs stateful recovery, review, and controlled publication.

output_examples.input: Create a private six-slide readiness course from our approved launch brief.
output: Resolved format: six slides with buyer context, value story, proof, objections, practice, and self-check.
Grounding: only claims and evidence from the approved launch brief.
Delivery: private interactive course with digital-human presentation and grounded learner questions.

output_examples.input: Our requested course exceeds the current slide limit. Keep it coherent.
output_examples.output: The course was recomposed to the account limit. The shorter sequence preserves the buyer story, approved proof, objections, and practice without truncating an outline.

output_examples.input: Publish the reviewed course for link sharing.
output_examples.output: The course is published with link access after a fresh state check. The returned share link is suitable for external learners.

best_practices: Provide current, approved source materials and identify the intended learner and business outcome.
Use private access unless broader distribution is explicitly required.
Review every outline, script, and visual checkpoint for factual support before advancing.
anti_patterns: Do not add unsupported customer results, competitive claims, pricing, or financial outcomes.
Do not upload agent-discovered files without naming each file and obtaining approval.
Do not create replacement runs to bypass failures, limits, or workflow conflicts.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates an interactive PersonWise course with designed slides, digital-human presentation, grounded voice questions, and optional assessments.

faq.question: Which source materials can it use?
faq.answer: It can use supplied text, user-selected documents, and approved reference images. Materials-only mode restricts the course to selected sources.

faq.question: Can it invent missing sales claims?
faq.answer: No. Unsupported claims, customer examples, competitive advantages, pricing, and outcomes must be omitted or routed to the responsible team.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the PersonWise CLI, browser OAuth, available credits, and network access to PersonWise services.

faq.question: How is course access handled?
faq.answer: Access defaults to private. Link access, publication, or Topics submission is used only when requested and permitted by current state.

faq.question: Can it resume an interrupted course?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads the current run and course state, follows allowed actions, and uses bounded waits or retries.
